title: Exact Symmetry as Algebra: Group-Structured Tensors that Enforce Physical Selection Rules
summary: Symmetry determines which physical responses of molecules and crystals are allowed and underlies many models used throughout the physical sciences. Yet several widely used machine-learned models learn symmetry only approximately from data, raising the question of whether approximate symmetry is sufficient for scientific prediction. Using the Orb-v3 force field, we show that it is often not: the relaxed space group of a crystal depends on the orientation of the input for $47\%$ of a $150$-crystal subsample, and relaxation lowers the space group for half of all $399$ crystals studied.
